stories.headline: Oil settles 5% higher as Trump and Iran trade war-compensation demands over Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Brent crude futures settled up $4.17, or 4.99%, at $87.72 a barrel on Aug. 10, while US West Texas Intermediate closed $3.95, or 5.05%, higher at $82.13 — the biggest percentage gains for both benchmarks since July 29.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent crude futures settled up $4.17, or 4.99%, at $87.72 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude futures closed $3.95, or 5.05%, at $82.13. The percentage gains were the highest since July 29 on both contracts.

key_facts.fact: The jump reversed last week's slide, when both benchmarks fell more than 7% on hopes Iran and Oman were near a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world's oil and LNG before the conflict began in late February.
key_facts.excerpt: Both benchmarks fell more than 7% last week on hopes that Iran and Oman were close to reaching a deal that would result in a reopening of the strait, which carried a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas before the start of the Middle East conflict in late February.

key_facts.fact: President Donald Trump said Iran must pay compensation for "all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded," countering Tehran's own demand for war reparations, an end to sanctions and the lifting of the US naval blockade before Hormuz reopens.
key_facts.excerpt: Iran also said the U.S. must lift sanctions on Tehran, and meet a number of other conditions for reopening the vital waterway, while U.S. President Donald Trump said Iran must pay compensation for "all of the people that they have killed and gravely wounded."

key_facts.fact: US Strategic Petroleum Reserve crude stocks fell by about 6.1 million barrels last week to 298.7 million barrels, the lowest level since January 1983, according to Department of Energy data.
key_facts.excerpt: On the U.S. supply side, stocks of crude oil in the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by about 6.1 million barrels to 298.7 million barrels last week, the lowest level since January 1983, according to data from the Department of Energy.

key_facts.fact: Consultancy Energy Aspects said on Aug. 10 that an average of only five vessels a day are transiting Hormuz, down from 14 a day after the June US-Iran memorandum of understanding, and Houthi militants claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery a day earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Energy Aspects said on Monday that only an average of five vessels are transiting through the strait, far below the 14 ships a day seen after the US and Iran reached a memorandum of understanding in June.

key_facts.fact: Brent was up about 16% versus pre-war levels, with shipping through the strait collapsing to between eight and 15 vessels a day in early August against roughly 130 transits before the conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: Between eight and 15 vessels crossed the strait on August 4, August 5 and August 6, according to ship-tracking platform MarineTraffic, a fraction of the roughly 130 transits before the conflict.

stories.headline: Archer Aviation to buy Boeing's Wisk, Insitu and SkyGrid; Boeing takes ~20% stake

key_facts.fact: Boeing and Archer Aviation announced on Aug. 10 that they signed definitive agreements for Archer to acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero (autonomous eVTOL), SkyGrid (airspace management software) and Insitu (military drones) subsidiaries.
key_facts.excerpt: The Boeing Company (NYSE: BA) and Archer Aviation Inc. (NYSE: ACHR) today announced the companies have signed definitive agreements in which Archer will acquire Boeing's Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu subsidiaries.

key_facts.fact: Insitu is a profitable defense business generating more than $200 million in annual revenue with operations across 35 countries; it has built more than 3,500 unmanned aircraft systems and is based in Bingen, Washington.
key_facts.excerpt: Insitu, based in Bingen, Klickitat County, and part of Boeing's defense business, has offices in the U.S., Australia, the UK and the UAE. It has manufactured more than 3,500 unmanned aircraft systems and generates $200 million in annual revenue, according to the news release published Monday.

key_facts.fact: The all-stock deal makes Boeing the largest outside shareholder in Archer with a near-20% stake; Boeing also agreed to invest up to $55 million in an upcoming Archer funding round, receives warrants for up to $200 million of stock and the right to nominate a board director.
key_facts.excerpt: Boeing has also agreed to invest up to $55 million in an upcoming Archer funding round and will receive warrants to purchase up to $200 million of the company's stock in the future.

key_facts.fact: Boeing keeps access to Wisk's core autonomous flight technology for current and next-generation commercial and defense aircraft through a technology-sharing arrangement, while Archer says the combination creates an "end-to-end physical AI platform" alongside its ZEE aerospace foundation model.
key_facts.excerpt: Combines Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu's pioneering autonomy and airspace intelligence software with Archer's leading purpose-built AI foundation model for aerospace and defense, ZEE.

key_facts.fact: Archer shares jumped about 20% to $6.69 on Aug. 10 while peers Joby (+2%) and EHang (-1%) barely moved and Boeing was roughly flat; Archer had entered the session down 26% year to date.
key_facts.excerpt: Archer Aviation (NYSE:ACHR) stock is surging 20% to $6.69 Monday morning after the eVTOL developer announced a landmark transaction with Boeing (NYSE:BA).

key_facts.fact: In Q2 results released the same day, Archer posted $5 million in revenue against a $263.2 million net loss and $1.56 billion in liquidity; Insitu alone would add more than the company's entire quarterly revenue once the deal closes by year-end, pending Hart-Scott-Rodino antitrust review.
key_facts.excerpt: That transaction, expected to close by year-end, would add more than $200 million in annual revenue from Insitu alone, a figure that dwarfs Archer's entire reported quarterly revenue of $5 million... The net loss widened to $263.2 million from $217.7 million the prior quarter... Archer ended the period with $1.56 billion in liquidity.

stories.headline: Brazil's inflation slows to 0.07% in July, pulling the 12-month rate back under the 4.5% ceiling

key_facts.fact: IBGE reported on Aug. 11 that the IPCA rose 0.07% in July, down from 0.16% in June — the lowest July reading since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: A inflação oficial do Brasil, medida pelo IPCA... desacelerou a 0,07% em julho, após marcar 0,16% em junho... A taxa de 0,07% é a menor para meses de julho em quatro anos, desde 2022.

key_facts.fact: The 12-month rate fell to 4.44% from 4.64%, back below the 4.5% upper bound of the central bank's tolerance band, after breaching the ceiling in May; the year-to-date increase is 3.44%.
key_facts.excerpt: No acumulado do ano, a inflação chega a 3,44%. Em 12 meses, o índice ficou em 4,44%, abaixo dos 4,64% registrados nos 12 meses anteriores e também do teto da meta de inflação, de 4,5%.

key_facts.fact: Housing was the biggest upward contributor, rising 0.99% as residential electricity accelerated to 3.09% in July from 1.53% in June.
key_facts.excerpt: O grupo Habitação teve a maior alta e o principal impacto sobre o índice, com avanço de 0,99% e contribuição de 0,15 ponto percentual. O resultado foi puxado principalmente pela energia elétrica residencial, que acelerou de 1,53% em junho para 3,09% em julho.

key_facts.fact: Food and beverages fell 0.67%, with tomatoes down 29.09%, potatoes down 19.59% and carrots down 14.41%.
key_facts.excerpt: Já o grupo Alimentação e Bebidas registrou queda de 0,67%... O tomate ficou 29,09% mais barato, a batata recuou 19,59% e a cenoura teve queda de 14,41%.

key_facts.fact: It was the fourth consecutive month of deceleration and the lowest monthly print since August 2025 (0.11%), matching the 0.07% median in the central bank's Focus survey published Aug. 10, which still sees 5.02% inflation for full-year 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: O boletim Focus desta segunda-feira (10)... projetava que a inflação de julho ficaria em 0,07%. Para o fim de 2026, o mercado espera IPCA em 5,02%... O resultado de julho foi o menor desde agosto de 2025, quando o IPCA marcou 0,11%.

stories.headline: Singapore lifts 2026 growth forecast to 4.5%-5.5%, crediting the global AI capex boom

key_facts.fact: Singapore's Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Aug. 11 that it expects GDP to grow 4.5% to 5.5% in 2026, sharply above its earlier 2% to 4% forecast.
key_facts.excerpt: The Ministry of Trade and Industry expects Singapore's economy to expand by 4.5 per cent to 5.5 per cent in 2026, sharply higher than the earlier forecast of 2 per cent to 4 per cent.

key_facts.fact: MTI permanent secretary Beh Swan Gin said at an Aug. 11 briefing that the global AI investment boom has been stronger than expected since the May forecast, providing significant tailwinds for AI-related production and exports.
key_facts.excerpt: Beh Swan Gin, permanent secretary at the Ministry of Trade and Industry, said at a virtual media briefing on Aug 11 that since the previous forecast in May, the global artificial intelligence investment boom has been stronger than expected.

key_facts.fact: It is the second upgrade to the outlook, which was set at 2%-4% in February before the outbreak of the war in Iran and originally at 1%-3% last year.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross domestic product is expected to come in at 4.5%-5.5% this year, the Ministry of Trade and Industry said on Tuesday, raising the 2%-4% estimate it set back in February before the outbreak of the war in Iran. It's the second upward revision to the growth outlook, which was initially set at 1%-3% last year.

key_facts.fact: Final second-quarter GDP came in at 5.9% year on year, above the 5.7% advance estimate, with manufacturing accelerating to 12.5% growth and first-half growth at 6.1%.
key_facts.excerpt: Singapore's economy grew by 5.9% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026... Goods-producing industries expanded 10.5% (vs 7.9% in Q1), as manufacturing growth accelerated to 12.5% from 7.3%... bringing first-half growth to 6.1%.

key_facts.fact: Key exports rose 27.4% in the second quarter on AI-driven demand for semiconductors and electronics, helping offset the drag from the Iran war and US tariffs.
key_facts.excerpt: Demand for semiconductors and electronic devices needed to power AI workloads at data centres worldwide has boomed in 2026, helping economies across Asia, including Singapore, mitigate the negative impacts of the Iran war and US trade tariffs.

key_facts.fact: Private economists moved with the government: Maybank raised its 2026 forecast to 5.2% from 4.8% and UOB to 5%, while RHB held at 4.5% citing remaining risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Maybank economists Chua Hak Bin and Brian Lee upgraded their 2026 GDP growth forecasts to 5.2 per cent from 4.8 per cent... UOB associate economist Jester Koh also upgraded his 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously.

stories.headline: Australia's central bank holds rates at 4.35% and keeps a tightening bias on oil-driven inflation

key_facts.fact: The Reserve Bank of Australia's Monetary Policy Board left the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35% on Aug. 11, after three increases earlier in 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: At its meeting today, the Board decided to leave the cash rate target unchanged at 4.35 per cent.

key_facts.fact: The board said inflation is "still too high" and is not expected to return to around the 2.5% midpoint of the target range until late 2027, warning it would raise rates further if upside risks materialise.
key_facts.excerpt: It is not expected to return to around the midpoint of the target range until late 2027 and there are upside risks to this projection... including increasing the cash rate target further if upside risks materialise.

key_facts.fact: The RBA cut its December headline inflation forecast to 3.6% from 4% and trimmed mean to 3.3% from 3.5%, after the oil shock from the Middle East conflict passed through less than feared; the decision was unanimous, reversing May's 8-1 split.
key_facts.excerpt: The RBA lowered its forecast for headline inflation to 3.6% by December, compared with its previous estimate of 4%... Its forecast for trimmed mean inflation... was also reduced to 3.3% from 3.5%. The decision was unanimous.

key_facts.fact: The bank said global oil supply will take time to recover and that higher fuel prices are being passed through to other goods and services, adding directly to inflation on top of domestic capacity pressures.
key_facts.excerpt: The disruption to global oil supply is adding directly to inflation and there are indications that higher fuel prices are being passed through to prices of other goods and services, so inflation is likely to remain high for some time.

key_facts.fact: The RBA noted that growth in Australia's major trading partners has been stronger than expected because the boost from AI-related investment has outweighed the adverse effects of the Middle East conflict.
key_facts.excerpt: So far, growth in Australias major trading partners has been stronger than expected, as the boost from AI-related investment has outweighed the adverse effects of the Middle East conflict.

stories.headline: MoonLake's nanobody sonelokimab hits every endpoint in Phase 3 psoriatic arthritis trial

key_facts.fact: MoonLake Immunotherapeutics said on Aug. 10 that the Phase 3 IZAR-1 trial of sonelokimab met all clinical endpoints at week 16 in biologic-naive adults with active psoriatic arthritis.
key_facts.excerpt: Phase 3 IZAR-1 trial in bio-naïve patients met all clinical endpoints at Week 16 for 60 mg sonelokimab

key_facts.fact: The primary endpoint was met with 42.1% of patients on 60 mg sonelokimab with induction achieving an ACR50 response, while 66.5% achieved ACR20, 41.2% reached minimal disease activity and 61% of those with skin involvement hit PASI90.
key_facts.excerpt: A total of 42.1% of biologic-naïve patients treated with sonelokimab 60 mg with induction achieved an ACR50 response... 66.5% of patients achieved ACR20, and 41.2% achieved MDA at Week 16. In patients with concomitant skin involvement, 61% achieved PASI90 at Week 16.

key_facts.fact: Under an unblinding protocol agreed with the FDA, only absolute response rates for the 60 mg arm were released; comparisons versus placebo stay blinded until the Phase 3 program completes, and the blinded safety analysis showed no new safety signals.
key_facts.excerpt: Consistent with the unblinding protocol defined with the FDA, topline disclosure at Week 16 includes absolute response levels and endpoint outcomes for the sonelokimab 60 mg with induction arm... The blinded safety analysis of IZAR-1 suggests a profile consistent with previous clinical studies and no new safety signals were observed.

key_facts.fact: IZAR-1 and IZAR-2 together enroll roughly 1,500 adults; IZAR-2 tests TNF-refractory patients against AbbVie's Skyrizi (risankizumab) and is expected to finish enrollment in Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The second trial, Izar-2, is being conducted in patients who have not seen improvement in symptoms after taking TNF inhibitors such as AbbVie's Humira, and it will directly compare sonelokimab with AbbVie's Skyrizi.

key_facts.fact: Alongside the data, MoonLake reported $537.0 million in cash and short-term securities at the end of Q2, a runway to mid-2028, and said it expects to file a Biologics License Application by the end of September 2026 for its lead indication.
key_facts.excerpt: MoonLake ended the second quarter with $537.0 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term marketable debt securities and expects to have a cash runway to mid-2028... End September 2026: Expected submission of Biologics License Application (BLA).

stories.headline: US appeals court lets thousands of youth-addiction suits against Meta, TikTok and Google proceed

key_facts.fact: The 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals ruled on Aug. 10 that Meta, Alphabet's Google, ByteDance's TikTok and Snap must face more than 3,000 federal lawsuits alleging they designed their platforms to be addictive to young users.
key_facts.excerpt: The San Francisco-based 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the companies' bid to reverse a lower court's ruling forcing them to face more than 3,000 lawsuits over the claims filed in federal court, concluding that the appeal came too early in the litigation.

key_facts.fact: The panel held that Section 230 of the 1996 Communications Decency Act provides a defense to liability, not immunity from being sued, making the companies' interlocutory appeal premature; Circuit Judge Jacqueline Nguyen wrote that Meta's implied-immunity argument fails.
key_facts.excerpt: "Although Section 230 does not expressly provide for immunity from suit, Meta argues that such immunity should be implied. We disagree," Circuit Judge Jacqueline Hong-Ngoc Nguyen wrote in her opinion.

key_facts.fact: The court also denied Meta's bid to postpone a trial brought by 29 state attorneys general alleging the company illegally collected children's data, designed platforms to keep young users hooked and misled consumers about safety.
key_facts.excerpt: The court also denied Meta's bid to postpone a trial beginning Wednesday in a lawsuit brought by 29 state attorneys general alleging that the company illegally collected and used children's data, designed their social media platforms to keep young users hooked, and misled consumers about their safety.

key_facts.fact: The federal cases — filed by states, municipalities, school districts and individuals — are centralized before US District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland; roughly 3,300 more are consolidated in California state court.
key_facts.excerpt: The cases, which have been centralized before U.S. District Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers in Oakland, California, seek damages, penalties and restitution from the companies... with approximately 3,300 of them in a consolidated proceeding in California state court.

key_facts.fact: The ruling adds to a string of losses: a Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent and awarded $6 million to a 20-year-old plaintiff, and a New Mexico jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million, with a judge last week adding $567 million for creating a public nuisance.
key_facts.excerpt: A Los Angeles jury in March found Meta and Google negligent for designing social media platforms that harm young people. The jury awarded $6 million... A jury in March ordered it to pay $375 million after finding it had misled consumers about the safety of its platforms. On Thursday, a judge found Meta had created a public nuisance and ordered it to pay an additional $567 million.
